title: New Terraform module: VPC network constructs, managed NAT/IGW, endpoints, and routing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Build a reusable Terraform module that codifies Redwood's VPC networking best practices for private deployments. Scope includes: multi-AZ subnet constructs (public, private with NAT, isolated), automatic NAT/IGW provisioning policies, S3/EC2/ECR/SSM VPC Endpoints (interface & gateway), route table management, and opinionated default route/routing table associations.

Goals:
- Provide a single module that teams can instantiate with minimal overrides to create compliant VPC networks for Private (VPC) deployments.
- Make safe, well-documented defaults (multi-AZ subnets, per-AZ NAT with optional shared NAT, tagging, flow logs).
- Support both cost-optimized and high-availability modes via a mode variable.
- Include upgrade and migration guidance so customers can adopt newer module versions without downtime or manual state surgery.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module (aws) with variables and outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids by type, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids.
- Feature flags: enable_s3_endpoint, enable_interface_endpoints (list), single_shared_nat (bool), ipv6_support (bool).
- CI tests (terratest) and example live deployment in test account.
- Confluence README + upgrade guide and automated migration helpers (state mapping examples).

Acceptance criteria:
- Module deploys in our test account across 3 AZs with HA NAT config by default.
- Automated tests validate: subnets created with correct CIDR splits, route tables correct for each subnet type, VPC endpoints reachable from private subnets, NAT egress works, and tagging conventions applied.
- Backwards-compatible upgrade path from module v0.x to v1.0 documented with step-by-step state actions.

Out of scope:
- Cross-account peering and Transit Gateway integration (will be separate module).
- Detailed network ACL rules beyond conservative defaults.
implementation_notes:
Technical approach: base module will use terraform-aws-modules patterns but implement Redwood specifics: explicit route_table per subnet type, per-AZ NAT Gateways with optional single shared NAT for cost mode, create aws_vpc_endpoint for gateway (S3, Dynamo), and aws_vpc_endpoint_interface for KMS/SSM/ECR/SecretsManager where requested. Use count/for_each driven by variables to keep state stable when toggling endpoints. Provide outputs consumed by higher-level private-deploy module.

Migration/upgrade plan notes: avoid renaming resources; use stable resource addresses and explicit lifecycle ignore_changes for attributes that change during upgrade (eg. allocation_id). Provide a migration helper script that maps old subnet tags to new module outputs. Recommend two-phase rollout for customers with live traffic: 1) deploy module in parallel (new resource names) and replicate route tables, 2) switch associations and decommission old resources.

Health checks: include a small optional null_resource that runs simple curl checks from a scheduled test instance (or Lambda) to verify S3 endpoint and external egress. Export CloudWatch metrics for NAT gateway byte counts and alarm when NAT error metrics spike.

Testing: use terratest suite to: deploy module, run connectivity checks, toggle enable_interface_endpoints, and validate module idempotence. Add drift detection via periodic plan in CI for the example stack.
